title: A simple, quantitative assay for the detection of viable but non-culturable (VBNC) bacteria
protocol: Grow up bacterial cultures in 3 mL of liquid media.
Standardize exponential-phase cultures to an OD of 0.100 with the media they are grown in.
Add 1.0 mL of the 0.100 OD culture to a microcentrifuge tube for use in cell staining.
Pipette immediately below the meniscus when diluting cultures.
Spread 10−5, 10−6, or 10−7 dilutions onto agar growth media from the standardized culture.
Incubate at optimal growth temperature.
Calculate colony forming units (CFU) per milliliter by multiplying CFU by the appropriate dilution factor.
Add 20 μL of 5× fixative to 80 μL of standardized 0.100 OD cultures into a microcentrifuge tube.
Mix well by finger vortexing.
Store the mixed culture at 4°C for up to one week.
Resuspend fixed cells using a micropipettor to ensure complete suspension.
Apply 20 μL of fixative-culture mixture to a Petroff-Hausser counting chamber.
Place the manufacturer-provided re-enforced cover slip on top of the chamber.
Allow 2 minutes for reduced capillary motion.
View chamber under a table-top phase-contrast microscope at 400× magnification.
Perform total cell counts in the highlighted diagonal boxes using the petroff-hausser counting chamber.
Count bacteria within each of the 16 smaller sub-quadrants in the grid.
Multiply the average number of cells in each of the 5 diagonal quadrants by 1.25 to adjust for the 5× fixative dilution.
Isolate colonies on a plate from counted cells.
Stain cells to detect live or dead cells.
Centrifuge the standardized 1.0 mL culture prepared in step 2 at 2,900 × g for 2 min.
Treat normalized cultures with stains for detection of live and dead cells.
Visualize treated cultures by fluorescence microscopy to enumerate percentage of living cells.
Photograph several hundred cells via differential interference contrast or phase contrast, and fluorescence microscopy using Cy3 or Texas Red and FITC filters across triplicate cultures.
